resources.string:
This application allows a remote operator to view this device's screen and to send touch input, text, and system navigation commands during a session only, over your local network or Bluetooth.

By enabling remote support you confirm that you are the owner of this device or that you have documented legal authorization from the owner, and that you consent to the operator seeing everything shown on the screen during the session.

How sessions work:
1. A 6-digit pairing code is generated and shown on this device. Only someone who can read this code can start a session.
2. A persistent notification is always displayed while remote support is listening or active. It names the operator and offers an End session action.
3. Screen streaming starts only after you explicitly accept the system screen-capture dialog. If you decline, no frames are sent.
4. During a session the operator can request this device's installed-app list (app name, package ID, version, and whether it is a system app). The list is sent only when requested, is never saved by either side, and the request and result count are recorded in the audit log.
5. You can end the session at any time from the notification; nothing keeps running afterwards.

ADB note: if USB debugging (ADB) is enabled, the optional hardening toggle below can refuse new sessions while ADB stays on. The default allows sessions with ADB enabled because operators often need ADB during legitimate support work.

Privacy: there are no external servers of any kind. Sessions travel through your local network or Bluetooth and are always AES-256-GCM encrypted. Audio is never recorded, files are never transferred, and screen frames exist only during an active session. The installed-app list is read-only metadata served only on request during a session.

Lets a consented operator for this device send taps, swipes, and text during a session you explicitly start.

E-Crew Remote Support can perform the following during a session that you explicitly start and can end at any time: observe the active window content, send taps and swipes, set text in focused fields, and trigger standard navigation actions (Back/Home/Recents/Notifications). It never processes events outside a session.
